title: Offline-First Local Synchronization Protocol with CRDTs, IndexedDB & Bidirectional WebSocket Streaming
problem: Collaborative productivity applications relying on synchronous cloud API calls freeze or throw network errors during intermittent connectivity, causing lost user edits and frustrating conflict modals upon reconnection. Centralized lock-based synchronization fails when multiple users edit overlapping document sections while disconnected. This project builds a production-grade offline-first collaborative synchronization engine in TypeScript. The system persists local document state in browser IndexedDB, executes optimistic mutations with sub-12ms write latency, streams binary state updates over WebSockets using Conflict-Free Replicated Data Types (CRDTs), and automatically resolves concurrent cross-device editing conflicts deterministically in Node.js and PostgreSQL.

use_cases.title: Mobile Field Operations Inspection & Work Order Sync
use_cases.first_sentence: Utility maintenance crews operating in underground vaults without cellular signals need to update equipment checklists and assign work tickets.
use_cases.second_sentence: The web app writes updates locally to IndexedDB, synchronizing conflict-free CRDT delta states over WebSockets once crew devices reconnect to base station networks.

use_cases.title: Multi-Author Collaborative Rich-Text Note Taking
use_cases.first_sentence: Remote teams collaborating across distributed time zones frequently co-edit documents while offline during travel or flights.
use_cases.second_sentence: The engine applies character-level CRDT operations locally, automatically converging document trees into identical states upon reconnection without overwriting peer edits.

use_cases.title: Retail Warehouse Point-of-Sale Inventory Management
use_cases.first_sentence: Retail store cashiers processing checkout queues during sudden network provider disruptions cannot afford checkout register freezes.
use_cases.second_sentence: The application records inventory decrements to local CRDT counter registers, guaranteeing deterministic eventual convergence across checkout lanes when network service restores.

hard_parts: Designing state-based or delta-mutator CRDT data structures that guarantee strong eventual consistency across out-of-order networks
Optimizing IndexedDB read and write transactions to achieve sub-12ms mutation persistence on mobile browser threads
Managing WebSocket connection reconnection state machines with exponential backoff and delta-vector catch-up exchanges
Compacting and garbage-collecting tombstone records in CRDT history logs to prevent unbounded storage bloat in PostgreSQL
screener_signals: Clean TypeScript codebase cleanly separating the IndexedDB storage adapter, CRDT math algorithms, and WebSocket network synchronizers
Multi-client concurrent chaos test suite verifying 100% state convergence across 50 simulated conflicting editing operations
Anti-fake verification script simulating two offline clients editing the exact same property simultaneously and verifying conflict-free convergence upon reconnection

architecture.data_flow: The user edits a document field; the client CRDT engine applies the change to memory and writes the mutation to IndexedDB in < 12ms; the UI updates optimistically; the sync manager checks WebSocket connection status; if online, the client computes a state vector delta and streams it over WebSockets; the Node.js server validates the message, writes it to PostgreSQL, and broadcasts the update to peers in the same room; receiving peers apply the delta to their local CRDT stores and write to IndexedDB; if offline, mutations queue locally in IndexedDB; upon reconnecting, the client and server exchange state vectors and synchronize missing deltas.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Mathematically commutative and associative CRDT merge functions eliminating merge order dependencies; vector clocks tracking causality.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: an offline-first collaborative synchronization platform in TypeScript with CRDTs, IndexedDB, WebSockets, and PostgreSQL.
worksheet.q2: Target users: frontend systems architects, distributed systems developers, and full-stack web engineers.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: field technician offline inspections, multi-author note taking, and warehouse point-of-sale inventory tracking.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 40 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 35 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 40.25 -> 40 hours. Advanced level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: CRDT commutative state-based vector design, sub-12ms IndexedDB persistence on mobile web threads, WebSocket reconnection state machines, and tombstone compaction.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: TypeScript editor scaffolding, IndexedDB wrapper, Node.js sync server, and chaos test suites. Synthetic document data only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: in-memory mock storage.
